summary: Space Mission Designer & Simulator is an interactive 3D aerospace engineering game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It bridges the gap between theoretical learning and hands-on mission design by allowing players to construct custom satellites, select scientific payloads, power systems, communications hardware, launch vehicles, and target orbits. During 3D flight simulation with real-time telemetry, players learn to balance competing NASA-aligned engineering constraints—such as mass limits, budgets, battery eclipse cycles, and data downlink throughput. By turning complex aerospace trade-offs into an engaging, interactive experience, the simulator fosters practical systems-engineering skills for students and space enthusiasts alike.
details: Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, Space Mission Designer & Simulator is an interactive, browser-based 3D aerospace engineering game that bridges theoretical learning with practical mission design. Players construct custom satellites—selecting structural platforms, scientific payloads, solar arrays, comms dishes, launch vehicles, and target orbits—while real-time resource indicators balance competing engineering constraints like mass limits, budgets, power generation, and data downlink throughput. Built with HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and Three.js (WebGL) for real-time 3D planetary rendering and orbital telemetry, the simulator features a persistent resource dashboard, full UA/EN localization, and two difficulty modes (Beginner with system hints vs. Engineer with$\Delta v$margins and battery Depth-of-Discharge calculations). By gamifying NASA-aligned systems engineering trade-offs, the project makes complex aerospace decision-making intuitive, visual, and engaging for students and space enthusiasts alike.
